representation: A reversible A to B reaction shown as a balance beam, paired forward/reverse rate bars, composition bars for A and B, and a K bar that responds only to temperature.
motion: adding A tilts the beam and raises the forward rate
the composition shifts right as B builds
rates converge and the beam levels at the new equilibrium
temperature changes K and the equilibrium composition
controls: reactant A added from 0 to 1 mol
checkpoints: adding A shifts the balance but not K
rates converge at a new equilibrium
misconceptionTest: The K bar is driven only by temperature, so adding A shifts the balance while K stays fixed. The rate bars remain nonzero when they become equal, so equilibrium is not reaction stopped. Raising temperature changes the K bar and the final composition, showing that temperature can change K while concentration cannot at fixed T.
accessibility: The beam, rate bars, composition bars and K bar are all text-labeled, both sliders are keyboard accessible, and alt text states that rates equalize and that K responds to temperature.
